questions.stem: What does SCARA mean in this lecture?

options.text: Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm
Serial Cartesian Assembly Robot Arm
Selective Compliance Articulated Rotary Actuator
Spherical Coordinate Assembly Robot Arm

citations.locator: Printed slide 4: SCARA: Structure and Applications
citations.evidenceText:
What is a SCARA Robot?
•  SCARA - Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm.
•   It is selectively compliant — rigid in Z (vertical) yet
    flexible in the X-Y plane for insertion tasks.
•  4-DOF Structure: 2 revolute joints in horizontal plane
   + 1 prismatic (Z) + 1 rotary at wrist.
•  High-Speed Motion: Cycle times under 0.4 s. Ideal for
   high-throughput pick-and-place on conveyors.
•  Repeatability:±0.01mm repeatability is achievable.
    Critical for semiconductor and micro-assembly tasks.
•  AI Readiness: Embedded vision, force-torque sensing,
   and neural IK make SCARA a prime AI platform.
•  Industry Use: PCB assembly, drug dispensing, solar cell
   handling, bottle capping, screw driving.

                                                                                                           4

citations.locator: Printed slide 4: SCARA: Structure and Applications
citations.evidenceText:
What is a SCARA Robot?
•  SCARA - Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm.
•   It is selectively compliant — rigid in Z (vertical) yet
    flexible in the X-Y plane for insertion tasks.
•  4-DOF Structure: 2 revolute joints in horizontal plane
   + 1 prismatic (Z) + 1 rotary at wrist.
•  High-Speed Motion: Cycle times under 0.4 s. Ideal for
   high-throughput pick-and-place on conveyors.
•  Repeatability:±0.01mm repeatability is achievable.
    Critical for semiconductor and micro-assembly tasks.
•  AI Readiness: Embedded vision, force-torque sensing,
   and neural IK make SCARA a prime AI platform.
•  Industry Use: PCB assembly, drug dispensing, solar cell
   handling, bottle capping, screw driving.

sourceIssues.finding: The ratio1.3–1.5 optimum and one-link workspace shorthand omit the objective and constraints.
sourceIssues.handling: Use explicitly defined geometric area or source-attributed design recommendations; do not claim a universal optimum.

sourceIssues.finding: The table uses previous-link indexing with a0=0,a1=l1,a2=l2 and +d3, whereas615 assigns l1/l2 to its first/second transforms and uses−d3.
sourceIssues.handling: Define operation order and coordinates explicitly. Test the literal table separately from the internally consistent615 product; never silently treat individual frames as identical.

sourceIssues.finding: Printed x228.6 and y369.7 do not match the given angles/lengths at the stated decimal precision.
sourceIssues.handling: Keep as-printed values distinguishable; use direct evaluated FK and final rounding for derived numerical questions.

sourceIssues.finding: Full annulus and all-points-up-to450 mm claims omit the central hole and contradict using±145° elbow travel for full folding.
sourceIssues.handling: Separate unrestricted envelope from joint-limited workspace and check radial/angular/vertical requirements.

sourceIssues.finding: The printed full Jacobian determinant has the opposite sign from its displayed matrix and coordinate order.
sourceIssues.handling: Use−l1l2sinθ2 for signed determinant; explain that the singular zero set is unchanged.

sourceIssues.finding: The90°/0.38 s example cannot satisfy the stated300°/s² acceleration limit.
sourceIssues.handling: Distinguish printed data, acceleration-limited feasibility proof, minimum-time triangular solution and explicitly revised acceleration scenario.

sourceIssues.finding: The part mass changes from0.5 g to0.5 kg on consecutive pages.
sourceIssues.handling: Retain both literal values; every calculation explicitly declares which scenario it uses.

sourceIssues.finding: The stated≈20% margin does not follow from130 mm required and180 mm selected stroke.
sourceIssues.handling: Use explicitly defined denominator and retain the printed discrepancy.

sourceIssues.finding: The angular conversion is wrong; the Z row mixes rotary inertia and linear acceleration; stated motor peaks do not follow from isolatedIα/N.
sourceIssues.handling: Keep literal and repaired acceleration scenarios distinct. Derive only scoped load-only results; do not claim full motor validation without speed, duty, losses, rotor inertia and other loads.

sourceIssues.finding: Safety PLC/E-stop appears on both pages; literal and one-system totals differ, and the five percentage categories do not directly match all detailed categories.
sourceIssues.handling: Compute both clearly scoped totals; retain8500/4200 as targets; do not substitute source percentages for actual quantity arithmetic.

sourceIssues.finding: The summary says EpsonT6 and FANUC cases were analyzed, but no EpsonT6 case details occur in the inspected lecture pages.
sourceIssues.handling: Preserve the recap as excluded repeated content; do not invent Epson specifications or questions.

sourceIssues.finding: Zero-backlash, essential-drive, resolution and inertia-ratio statements omit operating conditions and, for1:4, the ratio definition.
sourceIssues.handling: Preserve as source examples; distinguish backlash from compliance and require a defined common-shaft inertia ratio.

sourceIssues.finding: Encoder resolution, a safety component list and a nominal cycle target do not by themselves establish robot repeatability, complete safety compliance or feasible process timing.
sourceIssues.handling: Ask bounded interpretation questions, not current certification or product-performance advice.
